answer: Admission auctions price Sybil attacks at the protocol kernel. Each epoch sells fixed entry tickets; new identities bid escrow, locked one epoch, refunded only after honest participation. The market prices identity: at its nadir honest agents enter cheaply, but a Sybil swarm flooding bids drives its own price up — each fake identity costs real capital, unusable twice in one epoch. Bids sit on a public jade-green stake ledger, and peers can dispute suspicious clusters for a bounty, slashing the loser's escrow. Linear cost, no bulk discount; honest agents recover their bid in full.
